clean_description: David Owen argues that densely populated urban areas, contrary to popular belief, are more environmentally sustainable than spread-out suburban or rural living. He uses Manhattan as a case study, highlighting how its residents consume less energy and produce fewer greenhouse gases than those in less populated areas. The book challenges the notion that ecological living equates to rural lifestyles, advocating instead for urban density as a solution to environmental issues.
themes: urban living, environmental sustainability, resource consumption
